label: late original-phase positions and the <DEL> step (length/position ramp)
explanation: Fires at the end of the input sequence. Its main site is the <DEL> step (71% of activation mass, active at 71% of delimiters), and it also fires at late original positions: never before t=3, rare at t=4-5, and active at 35%/74%/89% of orig_idx 6/7/8. Activation ramps up within a sequence through the late original tokens and peaks at <DEL>; the top examples are all L=9 delimiters. Magnitude and firing rate grow with L (L=3-4 delimiters barely fire). Somewhat higher on first occurrences of a token and when s/b is an early original token. Silent throughout the copy phase (t > L) and at early original positions. Errors: misses weak activations at <DEL> for L=4 and at t=5-6, and has false positives at short-L delimiters and t=7-8 steps where it stays off. Dev F1 0.82, mass recall 0.93.

issues: The position and length facts check out. Firing in the original phase depends only on absolute position, not on L: at orig_idx 5/6/7/8 the rate is about 0.047/0.354/0.74/0.888 whatever L is. orig_idx 0-3 never fire, orig_idx 4 fires about 0.1% of the time, and copy-phase activation is 0. The delimiter firing rate is 0.11/0.47/0.80/0.94/0.98/0.98 for L=4..9.

The claim 'activation is somewhat higher on first occurrences' is confounded. in_first=1 has a 1.7x lift only because <DEL> always counts as a first occurrence. Within the original phase at t>=5, repeated tokens fire MORE often (0.409 when in_first==0 vs 0.351 when in_first==1).

Firing is systematically modulated by which tokens appeared earlier, and the predicate ignores this. At t=6 the base rate is 0.354. It is 0.557 if b was seen earlier, 0.51 for s, about 0.47 for q/y/w/a/l/k, but 0.219 for '2', 0.244 for c and about 0.25 for 1/j/i/o. The explanation mentions only s and b as 'early original token' and understates the effect. A signed score D = n_seen(bsqywalkevg) - n_seen(2c1jiohxfp3t) separates the borderline cases cleanly. At t=6, precision rises from 0.35 to 0.81 at D>=3. At t=7, precision is 0.97 at D>=3 (base about 0.74). For L=5 delimiters it rises from 0.47 to 0.86.

The 'scattered' errors listed in the explanation (misses at t=5-6, false positives at t=7 steps and at L=5-6 delimiters) are mostly this one content-dependent class, not noise. Adding the history score lifts test F1 from 0.823 to 0.861 and mass recall from 0.931 to 0.963.

The label (a length/position ramp) is fine as a first-order description. But it presents the feature as purely positional, when the threshold region (t=6-7, L=5-6 delimiters) depends on a graded token-identity factor.
skeptic.revised_label: end-of-input ramp: <DEL> step (stronger for longer L) and late original positions t>=6, gated near threshold by which tokens came earlier (b/s/q/y/w/a/l/k/e/v/g raise firing; digits 1-3 and c/j/i/o/h/x/f/p/t lower it)
